constraints.rationale:
Moral realism standardly requires that moral judgments be truth-apt beliefs, which is the core cognitivist claim.

Moral realism requires moral judgments to be truth-apt representations of moral facts, which commits one to cognitivism.

Moral realism conceptually requires that moral judgments express truth-apt beliefs (cognitivism) that correspond to objective facts.

Naturalist realism is explicitly a form of moral realism, identifying or grounding moral facts in natural facts.

Naturalist realism is analytically a sub-category of moral realism, distinguished specifically by its commitment to moral properties being natural ones.

Moral non-naturalism is standardly a realist view: there are objective moral facts or properties not reducible to natural facts.

In contemporary metaethics, non-naturalism asserts the existence of irreducible, mind-independent moral properties, making it a paradigmatic form of moral realism.
Moral realism posits that some substantive moral claims are true, whereas error theory holds that all such claims are systematically false.
Naturalist realism in 72 is a realist option; selecting it while choosing anti-realism in 14 is contradictory.
Non-naturalism in 72 is a paradigmatically realist position (mind-independent non-natural moral facts), so anti-realism in 14 is incompatible with selecting non-naturalism in 72.

Expressivism is a paradigmatic anti-realist metaethics, treating moral utterances as expressions of attitudes rather than describing mind-independent moral facts.

Expressivism treats moral judgments primarily as expressions of practical attitudes rather than representations of stance-independent moral facts.

Error theory denies any moral facts obtain, which is an anti-realist position.

Moral error theory denies that ordinary positive moral claims are true, so it is a paradigmatic moral anti-realist position.

Error theory presupposes moral claims are truth-apt (cognitivist) but systematically false.

Error theory requires cognitivism because it posits that moral judgments express beliefs, but that all such beliefs are systematically false.

Error theory says ordinary moral judgments are truth-apt beliefs that systematically fail to be true.

Presentism inherently privileges the present moment as the only temporal reality, which is the defining feature of the A-theory of time.

Presentism is a specific version of the A-theory of time which holds that only present objects and events exist.

Presentism requires an objectively privileged present, which is the central commitment of A-theoretic time.

Presentism gives the present an objective metaphysical privilege, which is a central A-theoretic commitment.

If zombies are metaphysically possible, physicalism about the mind is false, so non-physicalism follows.

If philosophical zombies are metaphysically possible, consciousness does not supervene on the physical, which is the standard refutation of physicalism.

If physical duplicates without consciousness are metaphysically possible, consciousness does not metaphysically supervene on the physical.

If physical duplicates without consciousness are metaphysically possible, then physical facts do not necessitate mental facts.

Mind-brain identity theory states mental states just are physical brain states, entailing physicalism about mind.

Mind-brain identity theory identifies conscious states with physical brain states.

The mind-brain identity theory identifies mental states with physical states.

Reliabilism is the paradigmatic externalist theory of epistemic justification.

Reliabilism about justification is the standard paradigm of epistemic externalism.

Reliabilism is the paradigm externalist theory of epistemic justification.
Transcendent universals are paradigmatic abstract objects, which nominalism explicitly denies.

Dualism about consciousness posits a mental ontology not exhausted by the physical.

Dualism about consciousness denies that the mental is wholly physical.
Mereological nihilism denies that composite objects exist, so a statue and a lump cannot be two distinct composite things.

The growing block theory posits an objective, moving edge of becoming (the present), which requires the dynamic A-theory of time.

The growing block view posits an objective edge of becoming, which is an A-theoretic feature.

Rationalism is fundamentally defined in epistemology by the acceptance of substantive a priori knowledge.

Epistemological rationalism is normally committed to at least some substantive a priori knowledge.

Rationalism about knowledge standardly requires some substantive a priori knowledge.
